---
title: "QC report — testing the gene table by community"
subtitle: "Exercise 1, notebook 04 · week 18 samples · DESeq2"
format: html
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(DESeq2)
library(patchwork)
library(ggrepel)

source(here("R/count_tables.R"))
d <- read_counts("instructional")

sample_groups <- read_csv(here("data/my_sample_groups.csv"))
metadata <- d$metadata |>
  left_join(sample_groups, by = "sample_id")

meta18  <- metadata |> filter(time_point == "week_18")
genes18 <- d$genes[, meta18$sample_id, drop = FALSE]

n18     <- ncol(genes18)
keep_g  <- rowSums(genes18 >= 10) >= ceiling(n18 / 4)
genes_f <- genes18[keep_g, ]

meta18$community <- relevel(factor(meta18$community), ref = "lactobacillus")

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(genes_f, meta18, design = ~ community)
dds <- DESeq(dds)
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("community", "anaerobe", "lactobacillus"))

out <- as.data.frame(res) |>
  rownames_to_column("feature") |>
  left_join(select(d$gene_info, ensembl_gene_id, symbol, gene_name),
            by = c("feature" = "ensembl_gene_id")) |>
  arrange(pvalue)
write_csv(out, here("data", "genes_by_community.csv"))
```

This report tests the gene table against the `community` grouping and checks
three things that go wrong silently:

1. **Sample order** — do count-matrix columns match metadata rows?
2. **Direction of the contrast** — does "positive log2FC" mean higher in anaerobe?
3. **Assumptions** — do the QC plots look like a healthy test?

The grouping was built from the **species** table in notebook 02, and is tested
here on the **gene** table — group and test never share a table.

# Sample order

```{r}
#| label: order-check
order_ok <- identical(colnames(genes18), meta18$sample_id)
stopifnot(order_ok)
cat("Columns match sample_id in order:", order_ok, "-", ncol(genes18), "samples\n")
```

The check is `identical(colnames(genes18), meta18$sample_id)`. It stops the
report if the names disagree, so nothing downstream can run on misaligned
data. DESeq2 pairs columns and rows by *position*, not by name, and never
warns if they differ — this one line is the protection.

```{r}
#| label: order-table
tibble(
  position     = 1:8,
  count_column = colnames(genes18)[1:8],
  metadata_id  = meta18$sample_id[1:8],
  same         = ifelse(count_column == metadata_id, "match", "MISMATCH")
)

ggplot(tibble(pos  = 1:157,
              match = colnames(genes18) == meta18$sample_id),
       aes(x = pos, y = 1, fill = match)) +
  geom_tile(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#0072B2", "FALSE" = "#D55E00")) +
  labs(x = "sample position (1 to 157)", y = NULL,
       title = "Every column matches its metadata row: all blue = pass") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
```

The table shows the first 8 positions agree name by name, and the bar below
checks all 157 positions the same way — all blue, so column *i* holds the
counts for the sample in row *i*.

# Group sizes

```{r}
#| label: group-sizes
counts_by_group <- dplyr::count(meta18, community)
counts_by_group

ggplot(counts_by_group, aes(community, n, fill = community)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(anaerobe = "#E69F00",
                               lactobacillus = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "week-18 samples",
       title = "37 anaerobe vs 120 lactobacillus: unbalanced but valid") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# The test

```{r}
#| label: deseq
resultsNames(dds)
summary(res)

res_df <- as.data.frame(res) |> rownames_to_column("feature")
sig <- filter(res_df, padj < 0.05)

tribble(
  ~quantity, ~n,
  "raw p-value < 0.05", sum(res_df$pvalue < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
  "padj < 0.05", nrow(sig),
  "padj < 0.05 & |log2FC| > 1 (more than two-fold)", sum(abs(sig$log2FoldChange) > 1),
  "of those: higher in anaerobe (LFC > 1)", sum(sig$log2FoldChange > 1),
  "of those: higher in lactobacillus (LFC < -1)", sum(sig$log2FoldChange < -1)
)
```

# QC images

## Size factors

```{r}
#| label: size-factors
sf <- sizeFactors(dds)
ggplot(enframe(sf, "sample_id", "size_factor"),
       aes(reorder(sample_id, size_factor), size_factor)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#0072B2") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "size factor",
       title = paste0("Range ", round(min(sf), 2), " to ",
                      round(max(sf), 2), " — bars far from 1 would be a worry")) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
```

## PCA: community against batch

```{r}
#| label: pca
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = FALSE)
pca_dat <- plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = "community", returnData = TRUE)
pct <- round(100 * attr(pca_dat, "percentVar"))

p1 <- ggplot(pca_dat, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = community)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_ellipse(linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(anaerobe = "#E69F00",
                                 lactobacillus = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(colour = "community",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", pct[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", pct[2], "%)")) +
  theme_minimal()

batch_vec <- meta18$rnaseq_batch[match(pca_dat$name, meta18$sample_id)]
p2 <- ggplot(pca_dat, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = batch_vec)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(colour = "rnaseq_batch",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", pct[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", pct[2], "%)")) +
  theme_minimal()

p1 + p2 + plot_annotation(title = "PCA of variance-stabilised counts")
```

Community separates on PC1; batch does not line up with that separation, so
the signal is not just a batch effect.

```{r}

  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#0072B2", colour = "white") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = nrow(res_df) / 50, linetype = "dashed",

```

## Volcano plot

```{r}
#| label: volcano
#| fig-height: 6
res_df <- res_df |>
  mutate(sig_label = case_when(
    padj < 0.05 &  log2FoldChange >  1 ~ "higher in anaerobe",
    padj < 0.05 &  log2FoldChange < -1 ~ "higher in lactobacillus",
    padj < 0.05                        ~ "significant, small change",
    TRUE                               ~ "not significant"))

# `out` already carries symbol and gene_name; res_df does not.
top10 <- slice_min(out, padj, n = 10)

ggplot(res_df, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(pvalue), colour = sig_label)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.9, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = top10, inherit.aes = FALSE,
             aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(pvalue)),
             colour = "black", size = 1.6) +
  geom_text_repel(data = top10, inherit.aes = FALSE,
                  aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(pvalue), label = symbol),
                  size = 2.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("not significant" = "grey80",
    "significant, small change" = "grey55",
    "higher in anaerobe" = "#E69F00",
    "higher in lactobacillus" = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(x = "fold change, anaerobe vs lactobacillus",
       y = "-log10 p-value", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

# Direction of the contrast

Two independent checks. First, boxplots of the six strongest genes: every
DESeq2 log2FC here is negative, so every box should sit higher in the
lactobacillus group.

```{r}
#| label: direction-boxplots
#| fig-height: 6
top6 <- slice_min(res_df, pvalue, n = 6)$feature

norm_counts <- counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)[top6, , drop = FALSE] |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("feature") |>
  pivot_longer(-feature, names_to = "sample_id", values_to = "count") |>
  left_join(meta18 |> select(sample_id, community), by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(select(out, feature, symbol), by = "feature")

# from `out`, which carries symbol; res_df does not
box_labels <- out |>
  filter(feature %in% top6) |>
  mutate(lab = paste0(symbol, "  (LFC ", round(log2FoldChange, 1), ")")) |>
  select(feature, lab)

norm_counts <- norm_counts |>
  left_join(box_labels, by = "feature")

ggplot(norm_counts, aes(community, count, fill = community)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ lab, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(anaerobe = "#E69F00",
                               lactobacillus = "#0072B2")) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "normalised counts (log10)",
       title = "Boxplots must agree with the sign of the log2FC") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Second, a numbers check: naive log2 ratio of raw group means against DESeq2's
log2FC. Exact values differ (DESeq2 works on normalised log counts and
shrinks fold changes), but the **sign must agree**.

```{r}
#| label: direction-table
check5 <- slice_min(res_df, pvalue, n = 5)$feature
t(sapply(check5, function(g) {
  m <- tapply(as.numeric(genes_f[g, ]), meta18$community, mean)
  c(naive_log2_ratio = round(log2(m["anaerobe"] / m["lactobacillus"]), 2),
    deseq2_LFC       = round(res_df$log2FoldChange[res_df$feature == g], 2))
})) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("feature") |>
  left_join(select(out, feature, symbol), by = "feature")
```

## What the significant genes are

```{r}
#| label: top-table
out |>
  filter(padj < 0.05, abs(log2FoldChange) > 1) |>
  slice_min(pvalue, n = 20) |>
  select(symbol, gene_name, log2FoldChange, padj) |>
  mutate(log2FoldChange = round(log2FoldChange, 2), padj = signif(padj, 3))
```

## Choices made

- Visit: week 18 only — alternative: all 471 samples with participant as a blocking term (rejected: the exercise asks for one visit and a simpler design).
- Grouping: `community` from notebook 02 (species table) — alternative: rebuild from the gene table (rejected: circular).
- Gene filter: ≥ 10 counts in ≥ 25% of samples — alternative: no filter (rejected: inflates the multiple-testing burden).
- Contrast reference: lactobacillus, so positive LFC = higher in anaerobe — alternative: default alphabetical levels (rejected: direction would depend on sort order).
- Normalisation: DESeq2 on raw counts — alternative: CPM (rejected: never for DESeq2).
- Significance headline: padj < 0.05 with |LFC| > 1 — alternative: padj < 0.1 alone (rejected for the headline; still visible in `summary(res)`).
- Samples dropped: none.
